turns.response:
Maybe because “coming of age” is imagined as a destination—one moment when you finally become settled, certain, and fully yourself. But there may be no permanent arrival. The feeling of being there can be real even if it passes; its passing doesn’t undo it.

Perhaps you aren’t failing to finish your story. Perhaps the story keeps making room for a self that is still changing. What would “being there” mean if it didn’t have to last forever?
